newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukrainian leader to visit Israel and Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian leader to visit Israel and Turkey.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma will visit Israel and Turkey from November 24 to 28 to boost political and trade relations, a senior Foreign Ministry official said on Saturday.

"The main focus of this first presidential visit to Israel and Turkey is further development of business cooperation, but, of course, Kuchma will discuss with his counterparts a wide range of political issues," Yuri Sergeyev told Reuters.

Kuchma is scheduled to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the first time during his two-day stay. He went to Israel for the funeral of the assassinated Yitzhak Rabin, who visited Ukraine last year as prime minister.

Ukraine had been gradually expanding trade ties with its southern neighbours. According to the Statistics Ministry, Ukraine has a positive trade balance for the first nine months of this year worth $18 million with Israel and $220 million with Turkey.
On a human level, Ukraine has a 500,000-strong Jewish comunity and while Israel is home to 300,000 immigrants from Ukraine.
Turkey has blood ties with 250,000 Tatars, Turkish-speaking Moslems, who live in Ukrain's Crimea peninsula.

After talks in Israel, Kuchma will leave for Ankara, where he will meet President Suleiman Demirel. The two governments are leading members of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC) organisation which promotes cooperation in fields ranging from transport to energy.
Ukrainian diplomats said about seven documents were being prepared for signature in Israel and 10 in Turkey.
